import math

# Data from Nonbanking Firms' Positions (Table FCP-I-1)
# December 1975, March 1976, June 1976, September 1976
belgian_francs = [12060, 2245, 16408, 13327]
canadian_dollars = [10371, 10724, 11175, 10806]

n = 4

# Calculate means
x_mean = sum(belgian_francs) / n
y_mean = sum(canadian_dollars) / n

print(f"Belgian Francs: {belgian_francs}")
print(f"Canadian Dollars: {canadian_dollars}")
print(f"Mean of Belgian Francs (x̄): {x_mean}")
print(f"Mean of Canadian Dollars (ȳ): {y_mean}")

# Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient
# r = Σ(x - x̄)(y - ȳ) / √[Σ(x - x̄)² × Σ(y - ȳ)²]

# Calculate numerator (covariance * n)
covariance_numerator = sum((belgian_francs[i] - x_mean) * (canadian_dollars[i] - y_mean) for i in range(n))
print(f"\nCovariance numerator (Σ(x - x̄)(y - ȳ)): {covariance_numerator}")

# Calculate denominator components
ss_x = sum((x - x_mean) ** 2 for x in belgian_francs)
ss_y = sum((y - y_mean) ** 2 for y in canadian_dollars)
print(f"SS_x (Σ(x - x̄)²): {ss_x}")
print(f"SS_y (Σ(y - ȳ)²): {ss_y}")

denominator = math.sqrt(ss_x * ss_y)
print(f"Denominator (√(SS_x × SS_y)): {denominator}")

# Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient
r = covariance_numerator / denominator
print(f"\nPearson correlation coefficient: {r}")
print(f"Rounded to 4 decimal places: {round(r, 4)}")
EOF
